To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maximum TRV and RRV levels for the series compensated lines are 2.2 times and 2.3 times higher respectively than those of the present network configuration.

the maximum TRV and RRVV levels are not significantly affected by the series compensation and that the maximum values of the TRV and the RRRV are not exceeded for any of the investigated fault conditions.
the transient recovery voltages and rates of rise of recovery voltages are well within the limits of the breakers, even for the worst case scenarios of out of phase tripping of clearing faults.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: - Analysis of the present 500 kV network without series compensation - Analysis of the future 500 kV series compensated network in 2006 with 20% compensation and in 2008 with 30% compensation - Comparison of TRV and RRVV levels of the above mentioned network configurations - Evaluation of the influence of various fault locations along the series compensated transmission lines - Analysis of the influence of the line breaker and switchgear types on TRV and RVRV levels
the following issues: - TRV and RRV at series compensated lines.
the TRV analysis at series compensated lines in Brazil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TRV and the RRRV at 40 kA breakers of the series compensated lines in Piauí are within acceptable limits and the existing circuit breakers can be operated safely under the new system conditions.
the TRV and RRVR levels at the 40 kA circuit breakers of the series compensated lines are not critical and that the present circuit breaker and switchgear design is suitable for these conditions.
the TRV and the RRRV levels for all the breakers under investigation are well within the breaking capability of the circuit breakers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the majority of the investigated fault conditions, the TRV level and RRRV level of the present system without series compensation is not significantly affected by the series compensation.
the TRV levels for the series compensated lines are higher than the present system configuration, and that the RRRV is not affected.
the TRV and the RRRV at 40 kA breakers are well within the limits for the present and future system conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

for the present system configuration the TRV at the 500 kV breakers is well below the TRV capability of 500 kV circuit breakers and therefore the breakers are not expected to be a limiting factor for the present system.
, in spite of the high levels of TRV and RRV that may occur, the existing 40kA circuit breakers are able to clear the short-circuit faults in all cases.
the TRV at the circuit breaker terminals is strongly influenced by the location of the short circuit fault and by the degree of series compensation.
